stances.claim: Despite public denunciation of the ICI as a diversion or 'palabas,' the commission and its members deserve a chance to live up to expectations of jailing the masterminds and recovering the billions plundered -- even as serious constitutional and operational questions linger.

It is unclear whether the words 'all government officials' in the ICI's mandate reach senators and congressmen, and whether -- and how -- the ICI can compel honorable lawmakers to be summoned, interrogated, arrested, or detained; without coercive power and supportive legislation, the ICI may simply be unable to prosecute them.

Biraogo v. Philippine Truth Commission (2010) declared EO 1 unconstitutional because it targeted only the 'previous regime' of Arroyo -- raising the question whether the ICI's prioritization of the 'last 10 years' might similarly fail the equal-protection clause.
stances.confidence: asked, not asserted, but doctrinally framed

stances.claim: The ICI risks adding an unnecessary bureaucratic layer that fades into a historical footnote, like the PCAGC (Ramos), PAGC (Arroyo), and PACC (Duterte) before it -- its findings being merely recommendatory and inevitably swamped by lawsuits.

stances.claim: Only the Office of the Ombudsman -- constitutionally insulated by a 7-year non-renewable term, impeachment-only removal, and salary protection -- possesses the mandate, powers, and independence required to run after trillion-peso plunderers; the ICI's real role is therefore to help and facilitate the OMB without interfering with it.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban responds to the TRILLION PESO MARCH and other rallies that denounced the Independent Commission for Infrastructure as a 'palabas' by extending the ICI a chance to prove itself, while listing the constitutional and operational questions that linger around its very creation. He asks whether 'all government officials' in the ICI mandate reaches senators and congressmen, whether lawmakers will accept being summoned, interrogated, arrested or detained, and whether Congress will pass laws giving the ICI subpoena, contempt, and arrest powers comparable to those it routinely deploys against legislative resource persons. He invokes Biraogo v. Philippine Truth Commission (Dec. 7, 2010, J. Jose Catral Mendoza, en banc) -- which struck down PNoy's EO 1 for equal-protection violation since it targeted only Arroyo's 'previous regime' -- to ask whether the ICI's prioritization of the 'last 10 years' may similarly fail the equal-protection clause. The ICI risks adding an unnecessary bureaucratic layer doomed to fade like Ramos's PCAGC, Arroyo's PAGC, and Duterte's PACC, especially since its findings are merely recommendatory and it will be swamped by lawsuits. By contrast, the OMB is constitutionally armed and insulated -- 7-year non-renewable term, impeachment-only removal, undiminishable salary -- with the Ombudsman vacancy since July 27 awaiting the JBC's super-final Oct. 6 vote and the President's 20-day window. CJ's bottom line: only the OMB can actually jail trillion-peso plunderers, and the ICI's real role is to help and facilitate that work without interfering with it.
